Exclusive: Zack Polanski says UK should defy Israel on fate of British Consulate in East Jerusalem
Green Party leader Zack Polanski has called on the British government to defy Israel and keep the British Consulate in East Jerusalem open, in comments made exclusively to Middle East Eye.
Polanski’s intervention will pile pressure on the Labour government not to comply with Israel’s order to close the consulate as the deadline for doing so, 8 October, approaches.
“East Jerusalem is illegally occupied Palestinian territory, and Israel has no sovereignty over it,” Polanski told MEE on Wednesday morning.
“The UK must ignore Israel’s order and keep the British Consulate open.”
Israel ordered the closure of the consulate in retaliation for British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband’s announcement of sweeping sanctions on Israeli settlements earlier this month.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Morocco appoints its first woman prime minister
data.author: MEE staff
data.summary:
Morocco appoints its first woman prime minister
Submitted by
MEE staff
on
Wed, 09/30/2026 - 11:05
Named by the king after her party’s victory in last week’s legislative elections, Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri now faces numerous challenges
Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri, Morocco's newly appointed head of government, arrives for a meeting in Rabat on 29 September 2026 (Abdel Majid Bziouat/AFP)
Off
Morocco’s King Mohammed VI has appointed Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri as head of the government, one week after her party won the legislative elections.
For the first time in its history, the North African kingdom will be led by a woman.
“This is truly a historic moment,” El Mansouri told public media after her audience at the royal palace.
“For the first time in our country’s history, a woman is taking on the responsibility of leading the government. This is not only a source of pride for me, but for all Moroccan women,” she added.
At 50, the lawyer becomes the thrid woman in the Arab world to reach this position, after Najla Bouden and Sarra Zaafarani in Tunisia.
El Mansouri had already made history by becoming, at just 33, the first woman to serve as mayor of the tourist city of Marrakesh in 2009 - a position she currently holds for a second term since 2021.
She had also made her mark during the 2023 earthquake, visiting affected communities repeatedly.
Currently the national coordinator of the Authenticity and Modernity Party (PAM), outgoing minister of housing and spatial planning, and a newly re-elected MP, El Mansouri had been widely tipped for the role in recent weeks.
However, without an absolute majority, the new prime minister will now need to form a coalition government for the next five years ahead of the 9 October parliamentary session.
A centre-right party, the PAM - part of the outgoing governing coalition - secured 97 of the 395 seats in the House of Representatives in an election marked by a turnout of just 38 percent, the lowest in nearly two decades.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Labour minister: British Muslims haven't always been heard but Burnham will change that
data.author: Imran Mulla
data.summary:

Submitted by

A reception at the Labour conference showed the government has turned a new page on engagement with Muslim civil society
The cake is cut at Equi's reception on Sunday evening at the Labour Party conference in Liverpool. (Imran Mulla/MEE)
Off
Not too long ago, British Muslim civil society barely engaged with the government. This was less because of British Muslims than because of the government itself.
The Conservative Party, who were ousted in 2024, made no particular attempt - especially after 2020 - to even appear to engage with mainstream Muslim organisations.
Fast forward to today and the situation has fundamentally transformed.
At the Labour Party conference, the widespread feeling among Muslims - both MPs and party members - was that things are looking up. "A new hope," as one parliamentary advisor called it, referencing Star Wars.
The reason: Andy Burnham.
Engagement with Muslims did improve under Keir Starmer's Labour government, but the relationship remained fraught: large numbers of Muslim voters abandoned Labour over its support for Israel during the Gaza genocide.
Under new Prime Minister Burnham, however, relations are better than they have been for decades.
This was in clear evidence at an event at the Hilton hotel at the Labour Party conference in Liverpool on Sunday evening.
Equi, a Muslim think tank, was celebrating its two-year anniversary.
The room was packed with representatives of Muslim civil society organisations, Labour members and several MPs.
"I had the privilege of being invited to the Foreign Office by the foreign secretary the day before he made the announcement on sanctions, on the Middle East," said Professor Javed Khan, Equi's director.

A legal team says the justice minister's decision is irrational and discriminatory, with 26 more cases in the pipeline
Displaced Palestinian university students hold up signs during a rally calling for easier travel to pursue education outside the Gaza Strip, in Gaza City on 20 April 2026 (AFP)
Off
When Hazem Faris, 19, received a full scholarship to study Computer Science at Ireland’s South East Technological University, it felt like he had the opportunity to “achieve a dream”, he said.
Faris lives in Gaza, and since 2023 he and his family have been forced to evacuate their homes eight times. However, when the Irish government denied Faris’s visa, his dreams became impossible.
Faris is one of the at least 103 Palestinian students who have had their visas rejected in Ireland this year, with visa approval rates dropping from 83.8 percent in 2025 to just 27.5 percent this year.
Last week, a team of lawyers challenged Minister of Justice Jim O’Callaghan’s refusal, asking him to reverse the decision.
The instructed barristers are Blinne Ni Ghralaigh, who represented South Africa at the International Court of Justice in its genocide case against Israel, and Eamonn Dornan. The solicitors include Sinead Marmion and Alannah Faulkner, alongside several junior counsel.
The legal action was launched last week, beginning with the case of Palestinian student Hafez Alrayyes, from Gaza.
Marmion said a further 26 cases are in the pipeline. “I think the other side is worried about the size and speed of [the case],” Marmion told Middle East Eye.
Marmion and her colleagues made an administrative appearance in the High Court on Tuesday, confirming that evidence and legal submissions will be with the court this week.

Influential Shia cleric Muqtada al-Sadr has said the US should compensate Iraqis for the damage inflicted on the country, as the last American troops pull out of Iraq.
In a statement on Wednesday, which is the deadline for American forces to end their 12-year presence in the country, Sadr hailed the "independence of Iraq" and praised those who fought against the US.
"We demand compensation from the American army for all the damages that occurred as a result of its occupation of Iraqi lands," he said.
"Everyone should file legal complaints regarding this."
The US first occupied Iraq in 2003 following the overthrow of Saddam Hussein, before pulling out its forces in 2011.
